title: Computer networks
description: OSI layers, TCP and UDP, the handshake, ports, DNS, ARP, subnets and HTTP status codes.

questions.prompt: At which OSI layer does IP routing between networks happen?
questions.explanation: Layer 3, the network layer, handles logical addressing (IP) and routing between networks. The data link layer (2) moves frames within one network.

questions.prompt: Which transport protocol guarantees that data arrives in order and without loss?
questions.explanation: TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmission. UDP sends independent datagrams with no delivery or ordering guarantee, which is why it has lower overhead.

questions.prompt: What is the default port for HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses 443. HTTP uses 80, and SSH uses 22.

options: Translates domain names into IP addresses
Maps IP addresses to MAC addresses
questions.explanation: DNS resolves names like example.com to IP addresses. DHCP assigns addresses, TLS encrypts, and ARP maps IP to MAC.

questions.prompt: How many usable host addresses does an IPv4 /24 subnet have?
questions.explanation: A /24 leaves 8 host bits: 2⁸ = 256 addresses. The all-zeros address (network) and all-ones address (broadcast) are reserved, leaving 254.

questions.prompt: What is the order of TCP's three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: The client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK. Both sides have then agreed on starting sequence numbers.

questions.prompt: On an IPv4 local network, which protocol finds the MAC address for a given IP address?
questions.explanation: ARP broadcasts "who has this IP?" and the owner replies with its MAC address. (IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery instead.)

questions.prompt: What does the HTTP status code 404 mean?
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found: the server has no resource at that URL. 403 is Forbidden, 301 is Moved Permanently, and 5xx codes are server errors.

questions.prompt: Which device forwards frames within a LAN based on MAC addresses?
questions.explanation: A switch learns which MAC address is on which port and forwards frames only there (layer 2). A hub repeats everything to every port, and a router forwards packets between networks by IP (layer 3).
/26 means 26 one-bits: 24 for the first three octets and 2 in the last: 11000000 = 192.
